authoritativeScope.apCoreScope: AP Precalculus Units 1-3 before the AP examination; Unit 4 remains optional supplemental enrichment.

transferProtocol.exceptionalGate: End of Week 17 with AP Unit 1-2 catch-up evidence and AP-pace independence

criteria.Evidence: Grade 9 readiness evidence + common Grade 10 diagnostic.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Correct obvious misplacements immediately before substantive AP content accumulates.

criteria.Evidence: Readiness Gateway 1 about 85%+ overall, about 80%+ on AP-extension items, all critical prerequisites secure, strong independent work; complete a short AP Unit 1 catch-up check if needed.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Transfer to Path A at the start of AP Unit 2. This is the cleanest in-year movement point.

criteria.Evidence: Very high cumulative mastery; AP-extension performance at AP pace; completion of AP Unit 1-2 catch-up modules; scheduling/AP exam implications resolved.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Transfer only when evidence shows the student can enter AP Unit 3 without sacrificing understanding. Otherwise remain in Path B and target Grade 11 AP.

criteria.Evidence: Continue common stretch tasks and AP-style benchmarks, but normally avoid changing sections late.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Protect continuity. A strong Path B student should finish the year as an exceptionally well-prepared Grade 11 AP Precalculus student.

transferProtocol.note: Important: Transfer decisions should use strand evidence, AP-pace independence, and completion of catch-up content—not only a course average. A student with a high average but unresolved factoring, function, or trigonometry gaps is likely to struggle after transfer.

pathA.title: Grade 10 Path A - AP Precalculus
pathA.destination: Complete AP Precalculus Units 1-3, the cumulative AP review/mock package, and selected calculus-bridge extensions E.1-E.4.

units.title: Polynomial and Rational Functions
units.intent: Develop covariational reasoning and polynomial/rational function analysis through graphical, numerical, analytical, and contextual representations.
units.phaseFocus: AP Topics 1.1-1.14; covariation and rates of change; polynomial/rational structure; zeros, end behavior, asymptotes/holes; transformations; model selection/construction.
units.implementationEvidence: Common Gateway A1 at end of unit; prerequisite micro-repair embedded, not a separate slow unit.

lessons.title: Change in Tandem
subtopics: Covariation; input/output quantities; increasing/decreasing behavior; contextual change; representation matching.
learningOutcomes: Describe how two quantities vary together; identify intervals of increase/decrease from multiple representations; communicate covariation precisely.

lessons.title: Rates of Change
subtopics: Average rate of change; secant slope; units; interval comparison; estimating local change from data/graphs.
learningOutcomes: Calculate and interpret average rates of change; compare rates across intervals; connect numerical rates to graph steepness and context.

lessons.title: Rates of Change in Linear and Quadratic Functions
subtopics: Constant vs changing rate; first/second differences; linear vs quadratic behavior; contextual interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish constant and changing rates; use first/second differences to classify behavior; justify a model family from rate structure.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions and Rates of Change
subtopics: Polynomial degree and rate patterns; local/global behavior; tables/graphs; regression-supported exploration.
learningOutcomes: Describe how rates change for polynomial functions; connect degree to qualitative behavior; interpret polynomial change in context.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions and Complex Zeros
subtopics: Real/complex zeros; conjugate pairs; factor form; multiplicity; graph connection.
learningOutcomes: Determine zeros from polynomial structure; use complex conjugate relationships for real-coefficient polynomials; connect real zeros/multiplicity to graph behavior.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions and End Behavior
subtopics: Leading term; degree parity; sign of leading coefficient; end behavior notation; global graph shape.
learningOutcomes: Determine end behavior analytically and graphically; use the leading term to predict behavior; connect equivalent forms to end behavior.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and End Behavior
subtopics: Degree comparison; horizontal/oblique end behavior; quotient interpretation; long-run model behavior.
learningOutcomes: Determine rational end behavior; identify an appropriate end-behavior model/asymptote; explain how numerator/denominator degree controls long-run behavior.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Zeros
subtopics: Zeros from numerator; domain restrictions; canceled factors; sign behavior.
learningOutcomes: Identify zeros of rational functions correctly; distinguish a zero from an excluded value; solve rational equations with domain awareness.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Vertical Asymptotes
subtopics: Denominator zeros after simplification; one-sided behavior; sign charts; graphical/numerical evidence.
learningOutcomes: Locate vertical asymptotes; describe one-sided behavior; justify asymptotes using simplified structure and nearby values.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Holes
subtopics: Common factors; removable discontinuities; hole coordinates; equivalent expressions vs functions.
learningOutcomes: Identify holes and their coordinates; explain why cancellation does not restore the excluded input; distinguish holes from asymptotes.

lessons.title: Equivalent Representations of Polynomial and Rational Expressions
subtopics: Expanded/factored forms; polynomial division; partial structural rewriting where useful; information revealed by form.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite expressions into strategically useful equivalent forms; select a form that reveals zeros, end behavior, or local features; verify equivalence and restrictions.

lessons.title: Transformations of Functions
subtopics: Translations; reflections; vertical/horizontal scaling; parameter effects; transformations across function families.
learningOutcomes: Construct transformed functions; predict graph changes from parameters; recover an equation from a transformed graph or contextual condition.

lessons.title: Function Model Selection and Assumption Articulation
subtopics: Regression candidates; residuals; data window; assumptions; interpolation/extrapolation; model limitations.
learningOutcomes: Select a defensible polynomial/rational model; use residual/context evidence; articulate assumptions and limitations with precise language.

lessons.title: Function Model Construction and Application
subtopics: Build models from conditions/data; regression; parameter interpretation; solve and apply model outputs.
learningOutcomes: Construct a function model; interpret parameters and numerical results; use the model to answer contextual questions and assess reasonableness.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.intent: Develop multiplicative-change reasoning, inverse/composition fluency, and data-modeling skills with exponential and logarithmic functions.
units.phaseFocus: AP Topics 2.1-2.15; sequences; exponential change; composition/inverses; logarithms; equations/inequalities; context/data modeling; semi-log plots.
units.implementationEvidence: Common Gateway A2; cumulative AP-style FRQ and calculator/non-calculator practice.

lessons.title: Change in Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
subtopics: Discrete functions; common difference/ratio; explicit forms; additive vs multiplicative change.
learningOutcomes: Represent arithmetic/geometric sequences as functions of whole-number inputs; interpret common difference/ratio; compare additive and multiplicative change.

lessons.title: Change in Linear and Exponential Functions
subtopics: Continuous extensions of sequences; constant difference vs constant ratio; growth factor; rate patterns.
learningOutcomes: Compare linear and exponential change; construct continuous function models related to sequences; explain why multiplicative change produces exponential behavior.

lessons.title: Exponential Functions
subtopics: Initial value; base/growth factor; domain/range; asymptote; monotonicity; transformations.
learningOutcomes: Describe key characteristics of exponential functions; construct an exponential function from conditions; interpret parameters in context.

lessons.title: Exponential Function Manipulation
subtopics: Exponent laws; equivalent bases; rational exponents; isolating parameters; strategically equivalent forms.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite exponential expressions into useful equivalent forms; apply exponent laws fluently; reveal growth factor, initial value, or comparison structure.

lessons.title: Exponential Function Context and Data Modeling
subtopics: Exponential regression; growth/decay; percent rate; doubling/halving interpretation; residuals.
learningOutcomes: Fit and interpret exponential models; convert between growth factor and percent rate; apply the model and evaluate fit.

lessons.title: Competing Function Model Validation
subtopics: Compare linear/quadratic/exponential models; residual plots; contextual plausibility; model selection.
learningOutcomes: Compare competing models using data, residuals, and context; justify a choice; identify when a model should be rejected.

lessons.title: Composition of Functions
subtopics: Composition notation; domains; process interpretation; multiple representations; modeling chains.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate and construct compositions; determine valid domains; interpret a composition as sequential processes in context.

lessons.title: Inverse Functions
subtopics: One-to-one behavior; inverse notation; graph reflection; domain/range exchange; verification by composition.
learningOutcomes: Determine and verify inverses; restrict domains when needed; connect inverse graphs and swapped domain/range.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Expressions
subtopics: Definition of logarithm; convert exponential/log forms; common/natural logs; exact values.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite between exponential and logarithmic forms; evaluate logarithms from known powers; interpret a logarithm as an exponent.

lessons.title: Inverses of Exponential Functions
subtopics: Logarithms as inverse functions; inverse graphs; domain/range/asymptotes; composition identities.
learningOutcomes: Construct inverse relationships for exponential functions; use logarithms to undo exponential processes; connect graphs and domains.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Functions
subtopics: Characteristics; transformations; vertical asymptote; increasing/decreasing behavior; multiple representations.
learningOutcomes: Describe and graph logarithmic functions; interpret parameters; identify domain, range, intercept behavior, and asymptote.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
subtopics: Product/quotient/power properties; change of base; equivalent forms; restrictions.
learningOutcomes: Expand/condense logarithmic expressions; use change of base; preserve domain restrictions while rewriting.

lessons.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities
subtopics: Common-base methods; logarithms; exact/numerical solutions; inequality reasoning; extraneous/domain checks.
learningOutcomes: Solve exponential/logarithmic equations and inequalities analytically or numerically; check domain conditions; interpret solutions in context.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Function Context and Data Modeling
subtopics: Logarithmic regression; diminishing growth contexts; parameter interpretation; residuals.
learningOutcomes: Fit and interpret logarithmic models; compare with alternative models; use the model to make and qualify predictions.

lessons.title: Semi-log Plots
subtopics: Log-scaled axis; exponential linearization; slope/intercept meaning in transformed scale; model validation.
learningOutcomes: Determine whether exponential behavior is plausible from a semi-log plot; construct/interpret linearization; connect transformed slope/intercept to exponential parameters.

units.title: Trigonometric and Polar Functions
units.intent: Develop periodic-function, trigonometric-identity, and polar-function reasoning with strong modeling and multiple-representation fluency.
units.phaseFocus: AP Topics 3.1-3.15; periodic phenomena; trig functions/graphs; sinusoidal modeling; inverse trig; equations/identities; polar coordinates/functions/rates.
units.implementationEvidence: Common Gateway A3; full Units 1-3 cumulative benchmark.

lessons.title: Periodic Phenomena
subtopics: Periodicity in context; cycles; period; repeated patterns; graphing a cycle; input/output interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Recognize periodic relationships; construct a graph from one cycle; interpret period and repeated behavior in context.

lessons.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
subtopics: Angles in standard position; radian measure; unit-circle definitions; signs by quadrant; tangent as ratio.
learningOutcomes: Define sine/cosine/tangent for angles; connect right-triangle and unit-circle meanings; determine signs and basic characteristics.

lessons.title: Sine and Cosine Function Values
subtopics: Exact unit-circle values; reference angles; symmetry; degrees/radians; technology-supported values.
learningOutcomes: Determine exact or approximate sine/cosine values; use symmetry/reference angles; move accurately between degree and radian measures.

lessons.title: Sine and Cosine Function Graphs
subtopics: Domain/range; period; zeros; extrema; midline; graph from unit-circle behavior.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret sine/cosine graphs; identify key features; connect graph locations to unit-circle coordinates.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Functions
subtopics: Amplitude; period; midline; phase/shift ideas; parameter interpretation; equivalent sinusoidal descriptions.
learningOutcomes: Analyze sinusoidal functions from equations/graphs; determine key parameters; write a sinusoidal function from features.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Function Transformations
subtopics: Horizontal/vertical shifts; amplitude/period changes; reflections; parameter effects.
learningOutcomes: Construct transformed sinusoidal functions; recover equations from graphs; explain parameter effects precisely.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
subtopics: Periodic data; sinusoidal regression; parameter meaning; assumptions; residuals.
learningOutcomes: Build a sinusoidal model from context/data; interpret amplitude, midline, period, and shift; judge fit and limitations.

lessons.title: The Tangent Function
subtopics: Graph; period; zeros; vertical asymptotes; transformations; contextual angle relationships.
learningOutcomes: Describe and graph tangent functions; identify asymptotes/period; solve or model accessible tangent relationships.

lessons.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
subtopics: Principal-value domains/ranges; arcsin/arccos/arctan; inverse graphs; compositions.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate inverse trig functions; use principal-value restrictions correctly; solve for angles and interpret inverse-trig outputs.

lessons.title: Trigonometric Equations and Inequalities
subtopics: General solutions over intervals; graph/algebra methods; inverse trig; periodic solution sets; inequalities.
learningOutcomes: Solve trig equations/inequalities on specified domains; use periodicity to generate solutions; verify graphically/numerically.

lessons.title: The Secant, Cosecant, and Cotangent Functions
subtopics: Reciprocal definitions; domains; asymptotes; graphs; relationships to sine/cosine/tangent.
learningOutcomes: Construct and analyze reciprocal trig functions; locate zeros/asymptotes; connect their graphs to the primary trig functions.

lessons.title: Equivalent Representations of Trigonometric Functions
subtopics: Pythagorean identities; sine/cosine sum identities; difference/double-angle consequences; identity verification; solving with equivalent forms.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite trigonometric expressions using required identities; verify identities; choose an equivalent form that simplifies an equation or reveals information.

lessons.title: Trigonometry and Polar Coordinates
subtopics: Polar system; multiple representations of a point; rectangular-polar conversion; complex numbers in polar form.
learningOutcomes: Locate points in both systems; convert coordinates accurately; explain nonuniqueness of polar coordinates; connect complex-plane and polar representations.

lessons.title: Polar Function Graphs
subtopics: r=f(theta); signed radius; domain restrictions; tables/technology; common polar behavior.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret polar graphs; connect changes in theta and r to motion in the plane; use domain restrictions to display intended portions.

lessons.title: Rates of Change in Polar Functions
subtopics: Increasing/decreasing signed radius; distance from origin; relative extrema; average rate of change of r with respect to theta.
learningOutcomes: Describe polar graph characteristics; compute/interpret average rate of change in radius per radian; connect extrema to relative distance from the origin.

units.title: Selected Post-Exam Calculus Bridge
units.intent: Use remaining instructional time on content with direct value for later calculus, rather than on low-priority topics.
units.phaseFocus: Selected parametric functions, planar motion, implicit relations, vector-valued thinking, advanced function analysis; no matrix-heavy core unless locally required.
units.implementationEvidence: Prepares later AP Calculus AB/BC without displacing tested AP Precalculus content.

lessons.title: Parametric Functions
subtopics: x(t), y(t); parameter domain; eliminating parameter when appropriate; orientation.
learningOutcomes: Represent planar curves parametrically; move between parametric and Cartesian descriptions when feasible; interpret the parameter.

lessons.title: Planar Motion with Parametric Functions
subtopics: Position components; tables/graphs; direction and time; contextual motion.
learningOutcomes: Interpret parametric position models; describe motion and orientation; connect component changes to overall movement.

lessons.title: Implicit Relations and Function Restrictions
subtopics: Implicitly defined curves; local function behavior; solving for branches; domain restrictions.
learningOutcomes: Interpret implicit relations; determine when a relation can represent y as a function locally; identify branches and restrictions.

lessons.title: Vector-Valued Function Preview
subtopics: 2D vectors; magnitude/direction; component form; r(t)=<x(t),y(t)>; connection to BC calculus vocabulary.
learningOutcomes: Represent motion with vectors; connect parametric and vector-valued notation; interpret components, magnitude, and direction conceptually.

requiredPackages.title: Cumulative AP Review & Exam Preparation
requiredPackages.focus: Spiral review by skill and representation; timed mixed MCQ/FRQ; regression/modeling; calculator fluency; error-driven reteaching.
requiredPackages.evidence: At least two full mock cycles plus targeted re-teach by strand.

supplementalUnits.title: Functions Involving Parameters, Vectors, and Matrices
supplementalUnits.classification: Supplemental/enrichment; not part of the required Path A lesson count

pathB.title: Grade 10 Path B - AP Readiness / Transition
pathB.destination: A rigorous prerequisite-and-bridge course leading directly to Grade 11 AP Precalculus, with evidence-based transfer eligibility into Path A.

units.title: Diagnostic & Precision Repair
units.intent: Create an evidence-based starting point and repair only the prerequisite skills that would otherwise block polynomial/rational, exponential/logarithmic, and trigonometric work.
units.phaseFocus: Entry diagnostic; algebra precision; function notation/domain; spot repair in systems and right-triangle trigonometry.
units.implementationEvidence: Targeted repair is limited to structural gaps that would block access to the bridge course.

lessons.title: Common Entry Diagnostic
subtopics: Linear/quadratic fluency; factoring; exponents/radicals; systems; function notation/domain/range; graph reading; right-triangle trig; calculator/non-calculator habits.
learningOutcomes: Identify strand-level strengths/gaps and establish an individual readiness profile.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Evidence is collected for each strand, including a small amount of written error analysis to distinguish conceptual gaps from carelessness or notation problems.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Coverage boundary: the diagnostic remains an assessment rather than a teaching or whole-class review period. Evidence from the diagnostic informs short-term flex groups.

lessons.title: Algebra Precision Repair
subtopics: Signs/fractions; exponent laws; equation transformations; factoring basics; radicals; notation; checking equivalence.
learningOutcomes: Execute core algebra accurately and explain why valid transformations preserve equivalence.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Expected endpoint: routine symbolic work is reliable, supported by mixed practice, error analysis, and non-calculator checks.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Coverage boundary: instruction returns to the core sequence once routine fluency is demonstrated. Multi-week Algebra 1 review and new AP modeling content are outside this phase.

lessons.title: Function Notation, Domain & Representations
subtopics: f(x); input/output; image/preimage; domain/range; interval notation; graph/table/formula/context; simple AROC language.
learningOutcomes: Interpret function notation/domains and move confidently among standard representations.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Students independently evaluate functions, interpret domain/range, read key graph/table information, and translate standard information among representations.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred content: full AP covariation, concavity-as-rate language, open graph construction from verbal scenarios, and dense multi-representation tasks.

lessons.title: Systems & Right-Triangle Trig Spot Repair
subtopics: 2x2 systems; accessible 3x3 elimination; Pythagorean theorem; sin/cos/tan; inverse trig in degrees.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate usable systems and right-triangle trig fluency for later modeling and trig work.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Focused repair is provided only where gaps are identified; the class benchmark confirms that these Grade 9 prerequisites are usable without scaffolding.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Coverage boundary: no new systems or unit-circle/trigonometric-function unit is included here. Radians and unit-circle work begin in R3.

units.title: Polynomial & Rational Foundations
units.intent: Develop the Algebra 2/precalculus foundations behind AP Unit 1 while explicitly reserving full AP covariation, equivalent-representation strategy, and open model construction.
units.phaseFocus: Rates; quadratic mastery; polynomial algebra, zeros, and end behavior; rational algebra/functions; transformations and model choice.
units.implementationEvidence: AP Unit 1 prerequisites and bridge foundations are established without completing AP Unit 1.

lessons.title: Rates of Change Foundations
subtopics: Slope/AROC; units; first differences; second differences; classify linear vs quadratic behavior from clear tables/graphs/formulas.
learningOutcomes: Compute and interpret average rates and recognize linear versus quadratic change patterns.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Compute and interpret AROC over intervals and use first/second differences to distinguish constant vs linearly changing rates in standard cases.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred to AP Precalculus: sustained change-in-tandem investigations, concavity from changing rates, polynomial rate-pattern analysis, and unfamiliar AP justification associated with Topics 1.1-1.4.

lessons.title: Quadratic Equation Mastery
subtopics: Factoring; completing square; quadratic formula; discriminant; real/complex solutions; checking.
learningOutcomes: Solve quadratic equations independently by an appropriate method and classify roots.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Choose an efficient solving method, solve accurately, classify roots, and connect discriminant information to the number/type of roots.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: AP-style open contextual model construction. This lesson emphasizes prerequisite fluency.

lessons.title: Quadratic Functions, Forms & Inequalities
subtopics: Standard/vertex/factored forms; vertex/intercepts; transformations; quadratic inequalities; basic model interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Analyze quadratic functions fluently and solve associated inequalities.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Move among forms, identify key features, solve quadratic inequalities, and connect algebraic form to graph behavior.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: AP-style rates-of-change arguments, complex model validation, and unfamiliar multi-representation tasks for AP.

lessons.title: Polynomial Operations & Factoring
subtopics: Add/subtract/multiply; special products; GCF; trinomials; grouping; sum/difference of cubes; solve factored equations.
learningOutcomes: Manipulate and factor polynomials accurately and use factored structure to solve equations.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Polynomial algebra is expected to be sufficiently fluent that later function analysis is not slowed by manipulation errors.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: the binomial theorem as a required topic and exotic contest-style factoring.

lessons.title: Polynomial Division & Theorems
subtopics: Long division; synthetic division; Remainder Theorem; Factor Theorem; quotient/remainder interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Use polynomial division and factor/remainder relationships accurately in standard cases.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Divide standard polynomials, evaluate remainders efficiently, and use the Factor Theorem to test/confirm zeros.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Full AP equivalent-representation strategy and slant-asymptote analysis are deferred; polynomial division remains a prerequisite tool.

lessons.title: Polynomial Zeros, Multiplicity & Complex Roots
subtopics: Factor-zero link; x-intercepts; multiplicity; crossing/touching; complex roots; conjugate pairs; degree/root count.
learningOutcomes: Determine zeros/multiplicities and predict crossing/touching behavior from algebraic structure.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Determine real/complex zeros in standard cases, interpret multiplicity, and predict local x-axis behavior from factor form.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: nonroutine AP tasks combining unknown coefficients, complex-zero constraints, multiple representations, and extended rationale.

lessons.title: Polynomial End Behavior & Standard Graph Construction
subtopics: Degree; leading coefficient; parity; end behavior; intercepts; multiplicity; rough graph; technology check.
learningOutcomes: Predict polynomial end behavior and build a defensible graph from algebraic features.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Predict end behavior and construct a reasonable sketch from major algebraic features, then use technology to verify rather than replace reasoning.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: formal limit notation, full AP polynomial rate-of-change analysis, and open model construction.

lessons.title: Rational Expressions & Equations
subtopics: Restrictions; simplification; operations; complex fractions at routine level; rational equations; excluded values; extraneous checks.
learningOutcomes: Manipulate rational expressions and solve rational equations without losing domain restrictions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Manipulate rational expressions and solve rational equations with explicit domain control and solution checking.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Course focus: algebraic fluency. Full rational-function AP analysis remains deferred to the AP course.

lessons.title: Rational Functions: Zeros, Holes & Asymptotes
subtopics: Factor/simplify; zeros; holes; vertical asymptotes; horizontal end behavior; intercepts; sign samples; standard sketch.
learningOutcomes: Analyze the essential algebraic and graphical features of standard rational functions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Distinguish canceled vs noncanceled factors, find standard asymptotes/holes/zeros, and sketch typical rational graphs from structure.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred to AP Precalculus: one-sided limit notation, required oblique/slant asymptotes, subtle end-behavior models, AP model construction, and dense multi-representation reasoning.

lessons.title: Transformations & Introductory Model Choice
subtopics: Translations/reflections/scaling; polynomial/rational parent structures; choose plausible family from clear graph/data/context; basic limitations.
learningOutcomes: Use transformations and make a defensible preliminary model choice from clear evidence.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Apply transformations and make a first-pass model-family choice when evidence is clear and the choice is structured.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: AP open model construction, cubic/quartic regression depth, piecewise model design, sophisticated residual validation, or extended written rationale.

units.title: Exponential & Logarithmic Foundations
units.intent: Build Algebra 2-to-precalculus fluency with multiplicative change, exponential and logarithmic functions, composition, inverses, and standard models while reserving full AP covariation and modeling depth.
units.phaseFocus: Sequences; exponent/radical fluency; exponential functions/models; composition/inverses; logarithms; equations; model comparison; semi-log preview.
units.implementationEvidence: AP Unit 2 prerequisites and bridge foundations are established while AP covariation and modeling depth remain reserved.

lessons.title: Arithmetic & Geometric Sequences
subtopics: Explicit/recursive rules; common difference/ratio; discrete domain; additive vs multiplicative change; sequence-function connection.
learningOutcomes: Represent sequences and distinguish additive from multiplicative change.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Write/interpret arithmetic and geometric rules and connect them to linear/exponential behavior in clear tables and contexts.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: AP-style change-in-tandem arguments, unfamiliar sequence modeling, series/sigma notation, or proof-heavy recurrence work.

lessons.title: Exponent Laws, Radicals & Rational Exponents
subtopics: Integer/rational exponents; radicals; equivalent forms; domain/sign awareness; simplifying and evaluating.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite and simplify radical/exponential expressions accurately and efficiently.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Students simplify/rewrite standard exponential/radical expressions accurately and move between radical and rational-exponent forms.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: AP parameter-inference and modeling tasks. This lesson emphasizes prerequisite fluency.

lessons.title: Exponential Functions & Transformations
subtopics: y=ab^x; initial value; base/factor; domain/range; horizontal asymptote; growth/decay; transformations; solve for simple parameters.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret standard exponential functions and transformations.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Construct, graph, and interpret standard exponential functions; identify parameter effects from familiar forms and clear conditions.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: AP-level parameter inference from dense tables/graphs, extended equivalent-form strategy, and multi-step model construction to AP.

lessons.title: Exponential Modeling
subtopics: Percent growth/decay; compound contexts; doubling/halving; regression; parameter interpretation; predictions; basic residual check.
learningOutcomes: Build and interpret standard exponential models and make reasonable predictions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Build standard exponential models from clear contexts/data and interpret initial value, factor, rate, and prediction limits.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: full competing-model validation, sophisticated residual arguments, or open AP data-model construction.

lessons.title: Composition of Functions
subtopics: Evaluate f(g(x)); symbolic/numeric composition; process chaining; standard domain restrictions; context interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate and construct standard compositions and interpret chained processes.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Students evaluate and construct routine compositions and identify obvious domain restrictions.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: complex contextual chains, nested compositions of unfamiliar functions, and AP representation switching for AP.

lessons.title: Inverse Functions
subtopics: One-to-one concept; horizontal line test; inverse notation; graph reflection; algebraic inverse; verify by composition; domain restriction when needed.
learningOutcomes: Determine, construct, and verify inverse functions in standard cases.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Find and verify inverses for linear, simple quadratic-with-restriction, exponential/log, and other standard one-to-one cases.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: subtle inverse domain/range analysis across unfamiliar representations or difficult contextual inverse modeling.

lessons.title: Logarithms as Inverses
subtopics: Exponential-log equivalence; common/natural logs; exact values; graphs; domain/range; vertical asymptote; basic transformations.
learningOutcomes: Use logarithms as inverse functions and interpret standard logarithmic graphs.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Rewrite between forms, evaluate common exact values, and graph/interpret standard logarithmic functions as inverses of exponentials.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: nonroutine AP logarithmic-function interpretation from unfamiliar representations and advanced model reasoning.

lessons.title: Logarithm Properties & Change of Base
subtopics: Product/quotient/power properties; expand/condense; change of base; domain restrictions.
learningOutcomes: Manipulate logarithmic expressions accurately while respecting domains.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Apply properties fluently and preserve valid domains; use change of base for numerical evaluation when appropriate.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: proof-heavy property derivations and symbolic drill beyond the needs of equations and modeling.

lessons.title: Exponential & Logarithmic Equations
subtopics: Common-base solving; isolate exponent; logs; exact/numerical solutions; extraneous/domain checks; straightforward contexts.
learningOutcomes: Solve exponential/logarithmic equations accurately and validate solutions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Solve standard exponential/log equations and interpret solutions in context, using technology when algebraic isolation does not yield a simple exact value.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: nonroutine inequalities and long AP multi-step contextual justification for AP.

lessons.title: Comparing Models & Regression
subtopics: Linear/quadratic/exponential/log comparison; rate pattern; regression; residual idea; parameter meaning; assumptions/limitations.
learningOutcomes: Select and justify a plausible model from structured evidence.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Choose a plausible family from structured evidence and use basic residual/graph/context evidence to justify a choice briefly.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: full AP competing-model validation, open model construction, or extended written argumentation.

lessons.title: Semi-Log Plot Preview
subtopics: Meaning of logarithmic scale; observe that exponential data can appear linear on semi-log display; technology demonstration.
learningOutcomes: Recognize why a semi-log plot can reveal exponential structure.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Students recognize the purpose of a semi-log display and identify the qualitative linearization idea from a prepared graph.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: construction of the transformed linear model, slope/intercept parameter recovery, proofs, or AP Topic 2.15 mastery.

units.title: Trigonometric & Polar Foundations
units.intent: Build the complete prerequisite and bridge structure needed to enter AP Unit 3 ready for conceptual trigonometric and polar reasoning.
units.phaseFocus: Radians; unit circle; trig values/graphs; sinusoidal models; tangent and reciprocal trig; inverse trig; equations; identities; polar foundations.
units.implementationEvidence: Entry readiness for AP Unit 3 is established; polar-rate work remains at preview depth.

lessons.title: Radians & Standard Position
subtopics: Degree-radian conversion; coterminal angles; standard position; quadrants; reference angles; arc-length concept.
learningOutcomes: Use radians and standard-position angle language confidently.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Use radians naturally, convert accurately, and determine standard-position/reference-angle information for common angles.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred content: full periodic-function covariation and unfamiliar AP contexts.

lessons.title: Unit Circle Coordinates & Special Angles
subtopics: Unit-circle coordinates; special angles; symmetry; signs by quadrant; exact values.
learningOutcomes: Determine exact unit-circle coordinates and trig values for standard angles.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Memorize/derive the special-angle coordinates and connect them to sine/cosine values without dependence on a calculator.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Full AP multiple-representation modeling is deferred; this lesson emphasizes prerequisite exact-value fluency.

lessons.title: Sine, Cosine & Tangent Values
subtopics: Unit-circle definitions; right-triangle connection; reference angles; exact/approximate values; tangent as ratio; signs.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate primary trig functions exactly or approximately and justify values/signs.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Evaluate sin/cos/tan for standard and calculator-supported angles and explain signs using quadrant/reference-angle reasoning.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: unfamiliar AP representation tasks and broader covariation interpretation for AP.

lessons.title: Parent Sine & Cosine Graphs
subtopics: Domain/range; period; zeros; extrema; midline; key points; unit-circle-to-graph connection.
learningOutcomes: Graph and analyze parent sine/cosine functions and connect them to unit-circle values.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Graph the parent functions from key values and identify essential periodic features.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: complex parameter recovery, open data modeling, and AP multi-representation graph analysis.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Transformations
subtopics: A sin(B(x-C))+D / cosine; amplitude; period; midline; horizontal shift; reflections; write equation from clear graph features.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret transformed sinusoidal functions from clear information.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Interpret parameters and construct transformed graphs/equations when features are clearly specified.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: difficult phase-shift conventions, ambiguous parameter recovery, and dense AP reasoning for AP.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Modeling
subtopics: Periodic contexts/data; choose sine/cosine; parameter meaning; simple regression; prediction; limitations.
learningOutcomes: Build and interpret standard sinusoidal models from structured evidence.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Build sinusoidal models from structured contexts or clearly periodic data and interpret parameters in context.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: open modeling from sparse/ambiguous data, residual-based model validation depth, or AP FRQ-style extended justification.

lessons.title: The Tangent Function
subtopics: Definition; period; zeros; vertical asymptotes; domain/range; parent graph; simple transformations.
learningOutcomes: Analyze the tangent function and its basic transformed graphs.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Graph and interpret the parent tangent function and simple transformations using unit-circle understanding.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not allocated instructional time: elaborate tangent modeling or difficult transformation recovery.

lessons.title: Secant, Cosecant & Cotangent
subtopics: Reciprocal/quotient relationships; parent graph features; asymptotes; domains/ranges; simple connections.
learningOutcomes: Recognize basic reciprocal trig functions and connect their features to primary trig functions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Recognize and sketch basic reciprocal trig graphs using sine/cosine/tangent structure.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: extended transformation/modeling treatment and high-complexity AP equivalent-representation tasks.

lessons.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
subtopics: Principal-value ranges; inverse notation; exact/simple approximate values; graph idea; solving for angles; compositions in standard cases.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate inverse trig functions correctly and use them to recover angles.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Use principal-value conventions correctly and evaluate inverse trig functions in exact/approximate standard cases.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred: difficult inverse-trig compositions and dense domain/range reasoning across unfamiliar representations for AP.

lessons.title: Trigonometric Equations
subtopics: Basic/transformed sine/cosine/tangent equations; specified intervals; periodic solutions; graph/numeric verification.
learningOutcomes: Solve standard trigonometric equations and verify solutions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Solve standard trig equations on given intervals and state general periodic solutions in accessible cases.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: a broad trig-inequalities unit or long identity transformations embedded in difficult equations.

lessons.title: Core Trigonometric Identities
subtopics: Reciprocal; quotient; Pythagorean identities; equivalent forms; simplification; use in equations; brief sum-identity exposure only if locally needed.
learningOutcomes: Use core identities to create equivalent forms and support standard solving.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Use the core identities as tools to rewrite expressions and support standard equation solving.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not included within this course: a proof-heavy identity unit; product-to-sum, half-angle, and lengthy identity proofs are outside the Path B priority unless locally mandated.

lessons.title: Polar Coordinates
subtopics: Polar grid; plot points; multiple equivalent coordinates; signed radius; rectangular-polar conversion; calculator entry.
learningOutcomes: Plot and convert polar/rectangular coordinates and interpret signed radius.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Plot and convert coordinates fluently and explain why multiple coordinate pairs can represent the same point.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred content: full polar-function family analysis and rates of change.

lessons.title: Polar Graphs & Rate Language Preview
subtopics: Use tables/technology for a few r=f(theta) graphs; signed radius; simple Δr/Δtheta from table; radial increase/decrease idea.
learningOutcomes: Enter AP able to recognize basic polar-function behavior and the meaning of average radial change per radian.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Recognize how a polar function generates points and understand average radial change at an intuitive/table level.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: AP polar graph analysis, model construction, relative extrema reasoning, and full Topic 3.15 rate-of-change requirements.

units.title: Function Synthesis & AP Transition
units.intent: Integrate the separate strands into the habits of thought AP Precalculus requires while introducing no new AP content.
units.phaseFocus: Transformations; composition/inverses; covariation; model selection; representations; cumulative readiness.
units.implementationEvidence: Prerequisite strands are integrated and common gaps that block AP pace are addressed.

lessons.title: Transformations Across Families
subtopics: Linear/quadratic/polynomial/rational/exponential/log/sinusoidal transformations; parameter effects; efficient graph construction.
learningOutcomes: Apply transformation reasoning flexibly across familiar function families.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Use transformation language flexibly and compare parameter effects across already-learned families.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: new function families and AP-only transformation cases. The synthesis uses familiar mathematics at moderate complexity.

lessons.title: Composition & Inverse Synthesis
subtopics: Nested but standard compositions; inverse verification; domain/range correspondence; choose useful form.
learningOutcomes: Use compositions and inverses efficiently across familiar function families.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Integrate composition/inverse skills across familiar function families and select an efficient approach.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred beyond this course: difficult contextual chains, subtle domains, or AP-level representation switching.

lessons.title: Covariation & Rates Across Families
subtopics: AROC; additive vs multiplicative change; periodic change; increasing/decreasing; extrema; compare rate behavior.
learningOutcomes: Compare how different function families change and communicate rate behavior clearly.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Describe how quantities change together in clear representations and compare rate structures across families.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred to the AP course: full AP Topic 1.1-1.3 covariation/concavity depth or dense unfamiliar-data reasoning.

lessons.title: Model Selection, Regression & Limitations
subtopics: Linear/quadratic/polynomial/exponential/log/sinusoidal models; regression; basic residuals; parameters; assumptions/limitations.
learningOutcomes: Select and defend a reasonable model and interpret its parameters/limitations.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Choose among familiar model families using structured data/context evidence and give a concise justification including limitations.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Not required within this course: full AP open model construction/validation, piecewise model design, or long written argumentation.

lessons.title: Multiple Representations & AP Habits
subtopics: Graph/table/formula/context translation; calculator vs non-calculator; concise rationale; timed mini-sets; notation precision.
learningOutcomes: Sustain multi-step reasoning across representations and communicate a concise rationale.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: AP-like formats are practiced using Path B mathematics, including short valid rationales and purposeful technology use.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Format familiarity is the goal rather than full AP difficulty. Extended instruction using released-AP complexity is reserved for the AP course.

lessons.title: Cumulative Readiness Studio
subtopics: Mixed retrieval; error analysis; targeted mini-lessons; student-selected practice; strand tracking.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate durable prerequisite mastery and select targeted practice independently.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Critical prerequisite strands are reassessed with independent error correction; reteaching is targeted to evidence of readiness-blocking gaps.
lessons.coverageBoundary: No new content is introduced. Isolated gaps are addressed through targeted support rather than reopening an entire unit.

lessons.title: Grade 11 AP Readiness Benchmark
subtopics: Common cumulative benchmark; non-calculator algebra; function reasoning; trig/log skills; representations; short rationale.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate that the prerequisite base is strong enough for Grade 11 AP Precalculus.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Produce a strand-level readiness report and identify any precise summer priorities before the AP launch preview.
lessons.coverageBoundary: This phase is limited to assessment and diagnosis; benchmark time does not add missing AP content.

units.title: AP Precalculus Launch
units.intent: Provide controlled familiarity with the organizing language and routines of AP Precalculus so Grade 11 begins smoothly, without duplicating the AP course.
units.phaseFocus: Controlled previews of AP Units 1-3; AP routines; final benchmark; summer bridge.
units.implementationEvidence: Familiarity with AP language and habits is established without pre-teaching the AP course.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Change in Tandem & Rates
subtopics: Covariation vocabulary; image/preimage; increasing/decreasing; AROC; graph-table-context translation; a few accessible opening-style tasks.
learningOutcomes: Understand the language and structure of the opening AP function/rate lessons.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Coverage includes AP language and problem structure through familiar functions and guided examples.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred to the AP course: the AP learning objectives, concavity/rate-development depth, or an AP Progress Check.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Polynomial/Rational Reasoning
subtopics: Integrated zeros/multiplicity/end behavior/asymptotes/holes/equivalent forms/transformations; one guided model discussion.
learningOutcomes: Recognize the structural questions AP asks about polynomial/rational functions.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Known ideas are revisited through an AP-like integrated investigation connecting algebraic structure to function behavior.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred content: slant-asymptote depth, full equivalent-representation strategy, open model construction, or FRQ complexity.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Exponential & Logarithmic Thinking
subtopics: Additive vs multiplicative change; equivalent exponential/log forms; model language; prepared semi-log visualization.
learningOutcomes: Recognize the organizing ideas that anchor AP Unit 2.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Familiar functions provide a preview of how AP organizes multiplicative change and representations.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred to AP Precalculus: new parameter-inference tasks, semi-log linearization mastery, and full model validation.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Trigonometric & Polar Thinking
subtopics: Periodic change; trig graph behavior; polar signed radius; one accessible rate comparison.
learningOutcomes: Recognize the organizing ideas and representations that anchor AP Unit 3.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Previously learned trigonometric and polar foundations are connected to AP language and multiple representations.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Deferred to AP Precalculus: additional sinusoidal-modeling depth, polar model construction, and full polar-rate analysis.

lessons.title: AP Mathematical Practices Familiarization
subtopics: Procedural/symbolic fluency; multiple representations; communication/reasoning; calculator selection; short timed sets.
learningOutcomes: Approach AP-style tasks with appropriate notation, representation choices, and concise reasoning.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Familiarization includes AP conventions for presenting known mathematics: precise notation, representation switching, brief rationale, and efficient technology use.
lessons.coverageBoundary: Outside current scope: full AP exam simulation and advanced content beyond the Path B curriculum.

lessons.title: Final AP Readiness Benchmark & Summer Bridge
subtopics: Cumulative benchmark; corrections; strand report; technology/non-calculator routines; personalized summer bridge.
learningOutcomes: Enter Grade 11 AP Precalculus with a clear readiness profile and no unidentified prerequisite gaps.
lessons.requiredPathBCoverage: Durable mastery is confirmed through corrections/explanations, with a precise summer plan limited to remaining gaps.
lessons.coverageBoundary: No new content follows the final benchmark. Remaining time is used for consolidation, targeted support, and transition planning rather than AP topics scheduled for the subsequent course.

requiredPackages.title: Gateway 1 - AP Transition Assessment
subtopics: Cumulative non-calculator algebra; graph/table/formula translation; polynomial/rational reasoning; short rationale; limited AP-extension section.
learningOutcomes: The evidence determines whether a student can enter the AP section at Unit 2 pace and identifies any catch-up requirements.
requiredPackages.requiredPathBCoverage: Evidence includes a common assessment plus independence and pace indicators. A strand report identifies the exact AP Unit 1 catch-up needed for transfer candidates.
requiredPackages.coverageBoundary: This is an assessment and decision point rather than an additional teaching week. A high average without structural fluency is not sufficient evidence for transfer.

requiredPackages.title: Gateway 2 - AP Transition Assessment
subtopics: Cumulative R1-R2; algebra; exponential/log functions; composition/inverses; modeling; limited AP-extension section.
learningOutcomes: Determine exceptional readiness for an AP Unit 3 entry or identify the strands to strengthen for Grade 11 AP.
requiredPackages.requiredPathBCoverage: Cumulative strand evidence is considered together with AP-pace independence. Transfer eligibility includes completion of AP Unit 1-2 catch-up requirements in addition to success in Path B material.
requiredPackages.coverageBoundary: This is an assessment point. Midyear transfer is reserved for exceptional cases in which catch-up does not compromise understanding or exam readiness.
